Ancestral Guardian

Some barbarians hail from cultures that revere their ancestors. These tribes teach that the warriors of the past linger in the world as mighty spirits, who can guide and protect the living. When a barbarian who follows this path rages, the barbarian contacts the spirit world and calls on these guardian spirits for aid.

Gain resistance to physical damage, and advantage on Strength checks and saves.

The first creature your attack on your turn is targeted by spectral warriors, which hinder its attacks.

Deals an additional [1] damage with melee and improvised weapons, and while throwing objects.

Has resistance to physical damage, and advantage on Strength checks and saving throws.

Cannot cast or concentrate on spells.

Ancestral Protectors: Causes creatures to have disadvantage and reduced damage on their attacks.

Battlerager

Known as Kuldjargh (literally "axe idiot") in Dwarvish, Battleragers are Dwarf followers of the gods of war and take the Path of the Battlerager. They specialize in wearing bulky, spiked armor and throwing themselves into combat, striking with their body itself and giving themselves over to the fury of battle.

You are a true axe idiot. Although some attempt to copy the almost-suicidal style of Dwarven combat, none can truly replicate your immense strength, durability and aggression.

Once in battle, you become almost animal-like, your eyes bulge, your teeth grind, and drool flicks from your mouth and beard. You were taught to use your whole body in combat, incorporating your spiked armor, which allows you to deal fatal blows with a barge, kick, or even headbutt.

While you are wearing medium metal armor and are Raging, you can use a Bonus Action to make one melee weapon Attack with your armor spikes against a target within [1] of you.

Additionally, when you use the Attack Action to Grapple or Throw a creature, the target takes [2] piercing damage if your Check succeeds.

Barbarians who walk the Path of the Beast draw their rage from a bestial spark burning within their souls. That beast bursts forth in the throes of rage, physically transforming the Barbarian.

Storm Herald

Barbarians who follow the Path of the Storm Herald learn to transform their rage into a mantle of primal magic that swirls around them. When in a fury, a Barbarian of this path taps into nature to create powerful, magical effects.

If you drop to [1] hit points while enraged, you regain [2] instead of being downed.

You still must make death saving throws, and you suffer the normal effects of taking damage while at 0 hit points. However, if you would die due to failed death saving throws, you don’t die until your rage ends, and you die then only if you still have 1 hit point.
